You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 3d39e1bb1c88f32820c5f9271f2c8c2fb9a52bac Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Oct 2018 11:33:34 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] wireless: airo: potential buffer overflow in sprintf()

It looks like we wanted to print a maximum of BSSList_rid.ssidLen bytes
of the ssid, but we accidentally use "%*s" (width) instead of "%.*s"
(precision) so if the ssid doesn't have a NUL terminator this could lead
to an overflow.

Static analysis.  Not tested.

Fixes: e174961ca1a0 ("net: convert print_mac to %pM")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Kalle Valo <kvalo@codeaurora.org>
---
 drivers/net/wireless/cisco/airo.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/cisco/airo.c b/drivers/net/wireless/cisco/airo.c
index 04dd7a936593..5512c7f73fce 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/cisco/airo.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/cisco/airo.c
@@ -5462,7 +5462,7 @@ static int proc_BSSList_open( struct inode *inode, struct file *file ) {
            we have to add a spin lock... */
 	rc = readBSSListRid(ai, doLoseSync, &BSSList_rid);
 	while(rc == 0 && BSSList_rid.index != cpu_to_le16(0xffff)) {
-		ptr += sprintf(ptr, "%pM %*s rssi = %d",
+		ptr += sprintf(ptr, "%pM %.*s rssi = %d",
 			       BSSList_rid.bssid,
 				(int)BSSList_rid.ssidLen,
 				BSSList_rid.ssid,
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by using the wrong format specifier in the `sprintf()` function. The original code used "%*s" which specifies a minimum field width, allowing for potential overflow if the string being printed (ssid) does not have a NUL terminator. The correct format specifier should have been "%.*s", which limits the number of characters printed to the specified precision (BSSList_rid.ssidLen), thus preventing a buffer overflow when the ssid is not properly terminated.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by using the wrong format specifier in the `sprintf()` function. The original code used "%*s" which specifies a minimum field width, allowing for potential overflow if the string being printed (ssid) does not have a NUL terminator. The correct format specifier should have been "%.*s", which limits the number of characters printed to the specified precision (BSSList_rid.ssidLen), thus preventing a buffer overflow when the ssid is not properly terminated.
